story: Continuing the recurring guidebook-listing boilerplate that repeats across entries, such as 'pm' after opening-hour times, '.co.uk' web addresses, and the ' MAP' in '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' tags.
Predicting the newline that starts a paragraph break right after sentence-final punctuation at the end of a description.
Completing multi-token proper names and rare words with their next subword piece the first time they appear (e.g. Marzoc-co, Blackf-ri-ars, Embank-ment, HISTOR-IC, Glou-cester).

Predicting the small connective or punctuation that follows a content word mid-sentence ('heart of', 'commissioned to', 'entry to', a comma after a clause), where that token has already occurred earlier in the passage.

Predicting the second half of familiar set phrases and names at their first occurrence ('Changing of the Guard', 'Book in advance', 'not hard to see why', starting a www. address) - a collocation-completion pattern the available fields cannot capture mechanically.
Predicting the determiner or common function word that follows a linking verb or possessive ('London has a', 'the academy has', "it's the", 'Carnaby St was the').
Spelling out the next subword piece of rare words, names, and all-caps category labels on their first appearance (MARK-ET, CLOTH-ING, Ros-etta, Hans-ard, hall-owed, plough-man).
Predicting an ordinary function word ('and', 'a', 'to', 'of', 'by') that keeps a plain prose sentence flowing after a determiner, bracket, or noun.
Predicting the article 'the' or 'a' immediately after a preposition ('tour of the', 'lost in the', 'run by a', 'from Limehouse to').
Continuing formatted items with punctuation or a short suffix: the 's' after decades like '1970s', the hyphen inside compounds like '300-year-old', and the '.' inside web addresses and prices.
Predicting ' MAP' after 'GOOGLE' in the constantly repeated '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' guidebook tag.
Predicting the comma, 'and', or semicolon that continues a list of items or qualities in descriptive prose ('oral histories and', 'medicinal plants and', 'a year,').
Predicting the main verb 'is' or 'was' after a long descriptive subject noun phrase ('This understated cathedral was', 'the only remotely chilled-out space ... is').
A loose grab-bag of continuations of addresses, postcodes, map-index entries, and set phrases, some copied from earlier in the passage - no single mechanical pattern picks these sites out.
Predicting the determiner or connective that follows a verb or comma in flowing sentences ('push open the', 'serves up ... in a', 'they still harbour a').
Predicting 'the' or 'a' after a preposition in guidebook prose, plus completing the sentence-opener 'Des-igned' seen in repeated listing intros.
Spelling out URLs and all-caps headings piece by piece (the 'OO' in G-OO-GLE, 'sandwich-river-bus', 'thenotting-hill', 'CAN-TER-BURY').
Predicting the connective or possessive that links clauses in long descriptive sentences ('and', 'this', 'its', 'for', 'includes') after a noun phrase.
Predicting an apostrophe continuation - possessive "'s" or a contraction ("'ll", "'d", "'re") - after a name, place, or pronoun ('Brighton's', "You'll", "you'd").
